I don't know what they'd charge for their charging stations. When you get a charging station installed at your home, then its consumption is added to your power bill and you pay the same amount. I believe when you buy a Tesla, you get free access to all their superchargers, but it's a luxury car with an appropriate price tag.

About winter, they do get on average 70 % of their effective charge (compared to summer use), but it's highly dependent on the type of battery (so it varies a lot from model to model) and the way you decide to heat the habitacle. Counter-intuitively, heating seats are a lot more power-effective than the fan heater.

The province of Quebec has about 5000 EV owners (about half of all the EVs in Canada as a whole), and their winters are comparable to Ontario's. If you understand French, Roulez électrique's website has a lot of information on EVs, and they're based in Quebec, so they are fully aware of our winter conditions.

If you don't drive too many long distances, you might be the ideal customer for an EV.

If you live close enough to Montreal, you can rent one at EEKO logical car rentals to try it out, all expenses included in the price (insurances, all charges, unlimited driving distance, etc.). I believe you can still call them to inquire about anything related to EVs, even if you're not close to Montreal or willing to rent one.
